transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I’m having trouble making myself make sense to people. Like at work, if I’m trying to explain the inventory numbers or who’s supposed to cover the weekend schedule, it starts out fine in my head, but then when I talk, my words kind of… jump. I’ll be talking about the truck delivery, then somehow I’m on Thursday, then the church grill, then my boss’s tone of voice, and I can see people looking at me like they’re waiting for the part that connects it all.

It’s frustrating because I know there’s a point in there. I’m not trying to be confusing. I’ve supervised people for a long time, so I’m used to giving directions and explaining things clearly. But lately it feels like the pieces come out in the wrong order, or with too many extra pieces stuck to them, and then everyone gets quiet or asks me to start over. That’s really why I’m here.

Can you describe what it feels like inside your head when your words start jumping like that? Are the thoughts coming too fast, do they feel disconnected, or does it feel like someone is inserting thoughts into your mind?

Inside my head it’s not exactly like… someone putting thoughts in there. I wouldn’t say it like that. It’s more like I have the whole thing in my head, like the inventory numbers and the weekend schedule, and I know I’m trying to get from one point to the next, but the path gets crowded.

Like I’ll start telling someone, “The truck came in short,” and then my mind jumps to Thursday because that’s when we usually fix the count, and then Thursday makes me think of the church grill because I was supposed to be there, and then I remember my boss’s voice when he asked about it, and suddenly I’m saying all those pieces out loud. To me they’re connected somehow, but I can see from people’s faces that I skipped the parts that would make it make sense.

It doesn’t feel fast like I’m excited or trying to talk over myself. It’s more… broken up, or sideways. Like the thoughts are linked by little things that make sense for half a second, but then I’ve already moved on and nobody else can follow where I went. Then I get embarrassed and try to explain more, but explaining more sometimes just adds more pieces.

You mentioned earlier that it doesn’t feel like someone is putting thoughts into your mind. Just to be sure, have you ever felt like your thoughts are being placed in your head by someone else, or that other people can hear your thoughts or are controlling them?

I don’t think so. I mean… I’ve tried to really think about that because it sounds like the kind of thing you’d want to know clearly, but I don’t have the sense that somebody is placing thoughts in my head like slipping a note under a door or anything like that.

And I don’t know that other people can hear my thoughts. Sometimes I get worried people can tell I’m confused, because their face changes or they stop talking and look at me, and then I start wondering how much of it shows on me. But that’s not the same as them hearing what I’m thinking, I don’t think.

As far as controlling them… no, not in the sense of somebody steering me. It feels more like my own thoughts, just not lining up right when I try to say them. Like they’re mine, but they don’t come out in the order I meant. So I guess my answer is no, not really those things.
Have you ever felt that people misinterpret your thoughts or words in a way that makes you feel like they’re twisting what you mean, even if you know you’re not being perfectly clear?

Yeah, I think that does happen, or at least it feels that way in the moment. Like I’ll be trying to say something pretty ordinary — inventory numbers, or the weekend schedule, just work things I should be able to explain — and I can tell I’m not saying it cleanly. I’ll start with the truck delivery being short, then I’ll mention Thursday because that’s when I thought we were going to fix the count, and then somehow I’m talking about the church grill or the way my boss said something, and people kind of freeze up.

And then it feels like they take the confused part and make that the whole meaning, if that makes sense. Like they think I’m making excuses, or changing the subject, or trying to be difficult, when really I’m trying to get to the point but the words are coming out in the wrong order. So yes, I do feel misunderstood. Maybe “twisting” is a strong word, because I know I’m not always giving them a straight line to follow, but it can feel like they’re hearing something different than what I mean. That’s the part that gets upsetting.
Have you ever had experiences where you believed something strongly, even when others told you it wasn’t true, and you felt like they were lying or trying to trick you?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way, no. I mean, I’ve definitely been stubborn before, like if I think I remember a schedule one way or I think someone said something to me at work, I can hold onto that for a while and argue my side. But that feels more like me trying to sort out what happened, not like I know for certain everyone else is lying.

The “trying to trick me” part… I don’t really think so. I get embarrassed and defensive when people correct me, especially if I already feel like I’m not explaining myself right, and then I might wonder if they’re making me look bad or if they’re not giving me a fair hearing. But I don’t have some fixed belief that they’re all lying to me or setting me up. It’s more confusion and frustration than that.

Sometimes afterward, when I calm down, I can think, “Okay, maybe I mixed that up,” or “Maybe I didn’t say it the way I thought I did.” So no, I can’t really think of a time where I believed something that strongly and just couldn’t accept anything else.
Have there been times when you believed something was definitely true, even when there was clear evidence it wasn't, or when other people strongly disagreed with you?

I don’t think so, not in that clear-cut way. I mean, I’ve been wrong about things, sure. I can dig in for a bit if I’m embarrassed or if I feel like people are jumping on me before I’ve finished explaining. Like if someone says, “No, that’s not what happened,” I might push back because in my head I’m still trying to line up the pieces and I don’t want to just fold right away.

But if there’s really clear evidence — like somebody shows me the schedule, or there’s a written note, or two or three people explain the same thing calmly — I usually can get to the point where I think, okay, maybe I had it mixed up. I may not like it. I might feel stupid or annoyed, especially if it happened in front of other people. But I don’t usually keep believing my version no matter what.

So… no, I can’t think of a time where I believed something was definitely true even after it was really obvious it wasn’t. It’s more that I get confused, and then defensive, and then later I can see maybe I was wrong or maybe I didn’t understand it right.
Have you ever experienced things that others don’t, like hearing voices or seeing things that aren’t there?

I don’t think so… not like that, anyway. I mean, I know people talk about hearing a voice when nobody’s there, or seeing a person in the room or something, and I can’t say that’s happened to me in a clear way.

There are times I’ll think I heard someone call my name at work, but then it’s just the store noise, carts, the intercom, people talking over each other — that kind of thing. Or I might glance at something in the corner of my eye and it’s just a coat rack or a shadow. But I think that happens to people, doesn’t it? I wouldn’t say I’m seeing things that aren’t there.

I guess I’d want to be careful how I answer, because sometimes I get unsure about what I heard if the room is busy or if I’m already stressed, but no, I haven’t had voices talking to me or things appearing that other people can’t see, at least not that I’ve noticed.

Have there been times when you believed something was true that other people around you didn’t believe, and you felt like they were wrong or missing something obvious, even if they tried to convince you otherwise?

I’m trying to think of an example, because the way you’re asking it sounds like maybe there’s supposed to be some big thing I was convinced of, and I don’t really have one that comes to mind.

I mean, I’ve definitely had situations where I felt like other people were missing what I thought was obvious, especially at work. Like if there’s a problem with how something is being handled, or I’m trying to explain why a decision doesn’t make sense, I can get pretty stuck on my point. And if people dismiss it too quickly, I can feel like, “No, you’re not listening, you’re not seeing the whole picture.” But that’s more like frustration or feeling unheard, not me believing some private truth that nobody else can see.

If they try to convince me otherwise, I might argue for a while. I know I can do that. I’ll go back over details, what was said, who was there, what the order of things was, and sometimes I probably over-explain because I’m trying to make them understand exactly what I mean. But if someone gives me a reasonable explanation, or shows me something concrete, I can usually step back from it. Maybe not immediately, and maybe not without feeling irritated, but I don’t think I stay convinced when everyone else has shown me I’m wrong.

So… I guess my answer is mostly no. I’ve felt misunderstood, or like people weren’t paying attention, but I don’t think I’ve had a strong belief that everyone else was wrong and I was the only one seeing the truth.

Have there been times when you believed something strongly about yourself or the world that other people didn’t seem to understand or agree with — something like having a special ability, being chosen for a specific purpose, or knowing something important that others didn’t?

No, I don’t think so. Not like being chosen, or having some special ability, or knowing some hidden important thing that other people don’t know. That doesn’t really fit me.

I mean, I’ve had times where I feel like I notice things other people miss, but I think that’s more from being a supervisor and having to pay attention to details — schedules, customers, who’s doing what, whether something’s going to cause a problem later. Sometimes I’ll think, “How is nobody else seeing this?” But I don’t mean that in a special way. It’s more frustration, like I feel responsible for keeping things straight and other people are being careless.

I don’t walk around thinking I have a purpose nobody understands, or that I’ve been selected for something. If anything, I usually feel like I’m just trying to keep up and not make mistakes. I might overthink things, and I can get pretty insistent when I believe I’m right, but I don’t think I’ve believed I had some unusual power or knowledge. Nothing like that comes to mind.
Have you ever felt like things in your environment, like TV shows, music, or things people say around you, are sending you hidden messages meant only for you?

No, I don’t think I’ve had that. I know what you mean — like thinking a song came on for a reason, or the TV is somehow talking to you specifically, or people nearby are saying something that’s meant as a message. I can’t say that’s happened to me in that way.

I mean, sometimes something will feel relevant because of what’s already on my mind. Like if I’m stressed about work and then I hear people talking about management or customers or someone “not doing their job,” I might notice it more, because it connects to what I’m already thinking about. Or if there’s a news story or a line in a show about someone being overwhelmed, I might think, “Yeah, that sounds familiar.” But I don’t take it as a hidden message to me personally.

With music too, sometimes a song reminds you of something, or the lyrics fit your mood, but I don’t think the radio is sending me anything. It’s more like my own mind making a connection after the fact. I can usually tell the difference between “this reminds me of my situation” and “this was meant for me,” if that makes sense.

And with people talking around me, if I’m in a store or break room and I hear bits and pieces, I might wonder for a second what they’re talking about, especially if I hear my name or something that sounds close to it. But I don’t think strangers or the TV or music are sending coded messages. I haven’t noticed anything like that.

Has there been a specific period of time, within the last few weeks or months, when you noticed a sudden and significant change in how well you could function at work or in social situations — for example, a time when things really started falling apart or you couldn’t keep up the way you used to?

Yeah… I think there has been a change. I don’t know if I’d call it “sudden” exactly, but over the last few weeks or months it’s become harder to ignore because other people are reacting to it now.

At work, the clearest thing is that I’m not really trusted to run the busy weekend shifts anymore. I used to do those, and even if they were stressful, that was part of my role. Now it feels like they’re steering those away from me, or making sure someone else is there in a way that didn’t used to happen. And after my performance review, my boss was pretty direct that if things don’t improve I could be suspended. That was… embarrassing, honestly. I tried to explain my side of things, because I don’t think everything was being looked at fairly, but the message I got was that they think I’m not keeping up the way I should.

And it’s not only work. At home, my wife has had to pick up things I used to handle — commitments, plans with people, that kind of thing — because apparently people have been getting uncomfortable or confused around me. I don’t always see it that way in the moment, but she’ll tell me afterward that something didn’t go well, or that someone didn’t know how to respond to me, and then she ends up smoothing it over or just handling it herself next time.

So yes, I guess things have been falling apart some. I don’t like saying it that way, but compared to how I used to function, especially at work and with people, there’s been a noticeable drop.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, especially around the same time these communication and work difficulties started?

I’m not really sure I’d describe it as feeling hopeless, exactly. I mean, I’ve been upset about what’s been happening, and embarrassed, and more stressed than I probably let on. When work starts going badly and my wife is having to step in with things, it does wear on you. So if you mean, have I felt discouraged by all of that, then yes, I suppose I have.

But I don’t know that it started as me losing interest in things first, if that makes sense. It feels more like the problems at work and with people came first, or at least they’re what I noticed first, and then my mood followed from that. I still can enjoy things sometimes if I’m not preoccupied, but it’s harder to settle into anything when I’m thinking about whether I said something wrong or whether people are seeing me differently.

So… down at times, yes. Hopeless, I don’t think I’d put it that strongly. Losing interest — maybe not in a clear way. It’s more that I’m distracted and worn out, and things don’t feel as easy or enjoyable because there’s all this pressure sitting on top of them.
Have there been times when you believed something was definitely true, even when there was clear evidence that it wasn’t, or when other people strongly disagreed with you?

I don’t know. I mean, “definitely true” is a strong way to put it. I can be stubborn, I guess, especially if I feel like someone is misunderstanding me or not seeing the whole picture. At work, for example, if people say I handled something wrong, I might feel pretty strongly that there’s more to it than they’re admitting, or that they’re judging me based on one piece of what happened. But I don’t know if that’s the same thing as believing something when there’s clear evidence it isn’t true.

Sometimes my wife will tell me I’m not looking at a situation the way other people are, and I’ll argue because, in the moment, my version of it feels reasonable to me. Then later I might think, well, maybe I was too sure of myself, or maybe I didn’t take in what they were saying. But I can’t think of a specific belief where everyone showed me proof and I just kept insisting no matter what.

So… I guess I’d say I’ve had disagreements where I held on pretty hard, and I may not always back down quickly. But I’m not sure I’ve had the kind of thing you’re asking about, where there was obvious evidence against it and I absolutely believed it anyway.

Have there been times when you believed something strongly about a real-life situation — like someone being unfaithful, being followed, or being poisoned — even though others told you there was no evidence to support it?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing, anyway.

I mean, I’ve had suspicions about things, sure, like anyone would. If someone at work is acting differently toward me, I might wonder if there’s something going on behind the scenes, or if people are talking about me in a way they’re not saying openly. But that’s more me trying to make sense of the tension, not me being absolutely convinced of something specific like being followed or poisoned.

And with my wife, no, I haven’t had some fixed belief that she’s being unfaithful or anything like that. If we argue, I may feel misunderstood or like she’s taking someone else’s side, but I’m not sitting there thinking there’s some secret affair or plot. Same with being poisoned — no, I haven’t believed that.

So I guess the answer is, I can get pretty locked into my interpretation of a situation, especially if I feel criticized, but I don’t think I’ve had one of those strong real-life beliefs where everyone says there’s no evidence and I still can’t let it go.
Have there been times when you believed something strongly, even when others showed you clear evidence that it wasn't true?

I’m not sure I can give you a clean example of that. I know you’ve asked it a couple different ways, and I’m trying to answer it honestly, not just say “no” because it sounds bad.

There have been times where I’ve been very sure of how I understood a situation, especially if it involved work or someone criticizing me. Like, if people were saying, “That’s not what happened,” or “You’re reading too much into it,” I might not accept that right away. I can go over and over the details in my head and feel like they’re missing something obvious. And when I’m in that state, I probably sound more certain than I really am.

But if you mean someone actually showed me clear proof — like something undeniable — and I still believed the opposite, I don’t think I can say that’s happened. Not that I remember. Usually it’s more murky than that, where people have different interpretations, and I get stuck defending mine.

So… I’d say I can be hard to convince sometimes, and I may hold on too tightly to my side of things, but I don’t know that I’ve believed something strongly in the face of clear evidence that it wasn’t true.

Have there been times when you believed something unusual about everyday situations — something that sounds possible but isn’t actually true, like thinking someone has been swapping your belongings or that your coworkers are secretly talking about you, even though there’s no clear proof?

I don’t think so… at least not that I would put in that category.

I mean, the coworker thing is tricky, because I have wondered if people were talking about me, but I don’t know that I believed it as a fact with no proof. In a workplace, people do talk, you know? Sometimes you walk into a room and people get quiet, or someone changes their tone, or you hear part of a conversation and your mind fills in the rest. I can get caught up in that and think, “Are they talking about me? Did someone say something about how I handled that?” But usually there’s some situation around it, like a disagreement or tension, not just out of nowhere.

The belongings thing, no, I haven’t had that. If I misplace something, I usually assume I misplaced it or someone moved it without thinking, not that there’s some hidden reason behind it.

So I guess I’d say I can read into everyday situations too much sometimes, especially if I’m already feeling criticized or on edge. But I don’t think I’ve had a firm belief like someone secretly swapping my things, or that coworkers were definitely plotting or talking about me with no evidence. It’s more wondering and overthinking than believing it for sure.
Have you ever had the feeling that random events, like something you saw on TV or something someone said in passing, were specifically related to you or had a special meaning just for you?

I don’t think so. I mean, I understand what you’re asking, I think — like if I’m watching the news and they say something, and I feel like it’s a message for me personally, or if someone makes a random comment in the grocery store and I think they’re secretly referring to my life. No, I can’t really say that happens.

Sometimes something will remind me of myself, of course. Like if there’s a TV show about a workplace argument, I might think, “That’s kind of like what happened with me,” and then I’ll sit there thinking about it longer than maybe I need to. Or if someone says something vague like, “Some people just don’t listen,” I might wonder for a second if they mean me, especially if I already feel tense or like I’ve done something wrong. But that’s more me being self-conscious or reading the room too closely, not feeling like the universe or the TV is sending me some special message.

So… no, not in the sense that random events have a special meaning just for me. I might overthink things, but I don’t usually take unrelated things as being specifically directed at me.
Have you ever felt like people’s conversations, actions, or things they said were secretly about you, even if they didn’t seem to be connected at first glance?

I don’t think I’ve felt that in a fixed way, no. I mean, I can think of situations where I wondered, briefly, if something was about me. Like at work, if two people stop talking when I walk by, or if someone says, “Well, some people need to follow the process,” and I had just been involved in some issue with procedure, I might think, “Are they talking about me?” But I don’t know that I’d say I truly believed it was secretly about me if there wasn’t some actual reason to connect it.

I’m probably sensitive to tone and timing, especially if I already feel like I’ve been criticized or I’m under a microscope. Then I can replay things — what someone said, how they looked, whether they paused too long — and I can make myself uncomfortable with it. But usually I can still step back and say, “Maybe that had nothing to do with me.” It might take me a little while to get there, but I can get there.

So if you mean conversations or actions that really had no obvious connection to me, and I felt sure they were secretly about me, I don’t think so. More like I sometimes worry or overread things when I’m already on edge.

So… no, I can’t think of a time where I believed something was definitely true even after it was really obvious it wasn’t. It’s more that I get confused, and then defensive, and then later I can see maybe I was wrong or maybe I didn’t understand it right.

Or I might glance at something in the corner of my eye and it’s just a coat rack or a shadow. But I think that happens to people, doesn’t it? I wouldn’t say I’m seeing things that aren’t there.

I guess I’d want to be careful how I answer, because sometimes I get unsure about what I heard if the room is busy or if I’m already stressed, but no, I haven’t had voices talking to me or things appearing that other people can’t see, at least not that I’ve noticed.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences delusions or overvalued ideas that do not meet the threshold for a delusion, which would help distinguish between schizophreniform disorder (F23.8) and other candidates.

I’m trying to think of an example, because the way you’re asking it sounds like maybe there’s supposed to be some big thing I was convinced of, and I don’t really have one that comes to mind.

I mean, I’ve definitely had situations where I felt like other people were missing what I thought was obvious, especially at work. Like if there’s a problem with how something is being handled, or I’m trying to explain why a decision doesn’t make sense, I can get pretty stuck on my point. And if people dismiss it too quickly, I can feel like, “No, you’re not listening, you’re not seeing the whole picture.” But that’s more like frustration or feeling unheard, not me believing some private truth that nobody else can see.

If they try to convince me otherwise, I might argue for a while. I know I can do that. I’ll go back over details, what was said, who was there, what the order of things was, and sometimes I probably over-explain because I’m trying to make them understand exactly what I mean. But if someone gives me a reasonable explanation, or shows me something concrete, I can usually step back from it. Maybe not immediately, and maybe not without feeling irritated, but I don’t think I stay convinced when everyone else has shown me I’m wrong.

So… I guess my answer is mostly no. I’ve felt misunderstood, or like people weren’t paying attention, but I don’t think I’ve had a strong belief that everyone else was wrong and I was the only one seeing the truth.

patient.answer:
No, I don’t think so. Not like being chosen, or having some special ability, or knowing some hidden important thing that other people don’t know. That doesn’t really fit me.

I mean, I’ve had times where I feel like I notice things other people miss, but I think that’s more from being a supervisor and having to pay attention to details — schedules, customers, who’s doing what, whether something’s going to cause a problem later. Sometimes I’ll think, “How is nobody else seeing this?” But I don’t mean that in a special way. It’s more frustration, like I feel responsible for keeping things straight and other people are being careless.

I don’t walk around thinking I have a purpose nobody understands, or that I’ve been selected for something. If anything, I usually feel like I’m just trying to keep up and not make mistakes. I might overthink things, and I can get pretty insistent when I believe I’m right, but I don’t think I’ve believed I had some unusual power or knowledge. Nothing like that comes to mind.

I mean, sometimes something will feel relevant because of what’s already on my mind. Like if I’m stressed about work and then I hear people talking about management or customers or someone “not doing their job,” I might notice it more, because it connects to what I’m already thinking about. Or if there’s a news story or a line in a show about someone being overwhelmed, I might think, “Yeah, that sounds familiar.” But I don’t take it as a hidden message to me personally.

With music too, sometimes a song reminds you of something, or the lyrics fit your mood, but I don’t think the radio is sending me anything. It’s more like my own mind making a connection after the fact. I can usually tell the difference between “this reminds me of my situation” and “this was meant for me,” if that makes sense.

And with people talking around me, if I’m in a store or break room and I hear bits and pieces, I might wonder for a second what they’re talking about, especially if I hear my name or something that sounds close to it. But I don’t think strangers or the TV or music are sending coded messages. I haven’t noticed anything like that.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think there has been a change. I don’t know if I’d call it “sudden” exactly, but over the last few weeks or months it’s become harder to ignore because other people are reacting to it now.

At work, the clearest thing is that I’m not really trusted to run the busy weekend shifts anymore. I used to do those, and even if they were stressful, that was part of my role. Now it feels like they’re steering those away from me, or making sure someone else is there in a way that didn’t used to happen. And after my performance review, my boss was pretty direct that if things don’t improve I could be suspended. That was… embarrassing, honestly. I tried to explain my side of things, because I don’t think everything was being looked at fairly, but the message I got was that they think I’m not keeping up the way I should.

And it’s not only work. At home, my wife has had to pick up things I used to handle — commitments, plans with people, that kind of thing — because apparently people have been getting uncomfortable or confused around me. I don’t always see it that way in the moment, but she’ll tell me afterward that something didn’t go well, or that someone didn’t know how to respond to me, and then she ends up smoothing it over or just handling it herself next time.

So yes, I guess things have been falling apart some. I don’t like saying it that way, but compared to how I used to function, especially at work and with people, there’s been a noticeable drop.

So… down at times, yes. Hopeless, I don’t think I’d put it that strongly. Losing interest — maybe not in a clear way. It’s more that I’m distracted and worn out, and things don’t feel as easy or enjoyable because there’s all this pressure sitting on top of them.
